Restored 1964 Chevy Corvette Selling at No Reserve, Price Already Going Through the Roof
21 photos
Photo: eBay seller mcqueen930
51 bids and a top offer that already surpasses $50,000. This is all you need to know about this 1964 Chevrolet Corvette that’s selling at no reserve on eBay. The auction is now in the final two days, and what we know for sure is that the car will leave for a new garage shortly.
The vehicle has already been restored, and this is probably why so many people are trying to get their hands on it. It doesn’t seem to need anything, as it’s in good shape and doesn’t suffer from any rust problems. Before you head over to the comments section to post the typical fiberglass comment, the no-rust promise concerns the frame specifically, which, according to the seller, is as clean as it can be.
This two-owner Corvette was originally purchased by a gentleman named Tom in Las Vegas, Nevada. Tom kept the car for no more, no less than 45 years, and he always babied this Corvette, parking it in his garage in the state of Nevada. This is good news from a rust perspective, as these cars don’t typically struggle with the invasion of rust.
Another gentleman named Ed Watson bought the car in 2009 and immediately started a complete restoration. He spent over $40K to get the Corvette in the condition you can see today. Since the restoration was finalized, the car was parked in a garage, away from anything that could compromise its shape.
Photo: eBay seller mcqueen930 Chevrolet produced 22,229 Corvettes for the 1964 model year, and the coupe accounted for only 8,304 cars. With the split-window design now gone, the coupe is less desirable than its 1963 sibling, though the special thing that sets a 1964 apart from the rest of the crowd is the new hood.
Chevrolet also introduced a new Satin Silver finish, while the engine lineup included not one, not two, but four different configurations.
It all started with the base 327, which produced 250 horsepower. The L75 was the first optional engine, being upgraded to 300 horsepower. The L76 and the L84 were the top choices, but despite sporting the same displacement, they benefitted from a higher compression ratio and mechanical valve lifters.
These updates resulted in a notable power increase to 365 and 375 horsepower, respectively.
Photo: eBay seller mcqueen930 The L84 used fuel injection and carried an extra price tag of no more, no less than $538. It was an expensive upgrade that only 6% of Corvette buyers ended up getting, so if you somehow come across a genuine L84-powered specimen, you’d better not miss the opportunity to get it.
Otherwise, this Corvette has a period-correct 327, but it is no longer original. We’re not getting any other specifics, so if you’re interested in buying this car, you’d better do yourself a favor and ask more questions before making an offer.
The new 327 is paired with the original Powerglide transmission “that shifts perfectly,” as the owner explains. The car is already in tip-top shape from a mechanical perspective, so you can fly in and drive home if you don’t want to pay the extra shipping costs.
The paint was refreshed as part of the refresh, and the seller promises that you won’t find any cracks or any other problems in the paint or the fiberglass. The interior is also in good shape, and the driver and the passenger seats are said to be in perfect condition.
Unfortunately, this Corvette has also received an aftermarket upgrade, so it’s now fitted with a vintage AM/FM radio with AUX and rear speakers. You can always undo this change if you’d rather prefer to stick with the original settings - and please, do that because these cars shouldn’t get modern upgrades, considering they’re all about those fantastic classic car times.
Photo: eBay seller mcqueen930 The Corvette is also equipped with power steering and power brakes, as well as with air conditioning. Oddly, air conditioning and power brakes were rare options. Air conditioning carried an extra price tag of no more, no less than $421, so only 8.9% of the Vette buyers agreed to pay that much for a climate-controlled cabin in 1964.
Power brakes were significantly more affordable at $43.05, but only 10.2% of the Corvettes ended up being fitted with this special stopping power.
The battle for this Corvette is impressively fierce, and considering this is a no-reserve auction, meaning that the highest bidder takes it home when it all comes to an end, more bidders could join at the very last minute.
The top offer at the time of press is $50,200, and the Corvette landed on the watchlists of $41 people. The listing will go offline in a little over 2 days, so be prepared for some very intense final minutes of the auction.
The car is parked in Winter Garden, Florida, and it should be able to go anywhere on its wheels.
